drafted_from: tools/pin-files-by-content/tool-rows.json (tool:check-quotes-against-their-source-bytes), do-work/verify-source-spans.mjs, test/verify-source-spans.test.mjs; the example was run on synthetic files
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check that each quote in my bindings.json is still the exact text at its byte range in menu.txt, and write the report to a new file." It runs verify-source-spans.mjs and names every quote position that failed.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads one bindings manifest and the source files it names, and writes one new report file.
instructions: 1. Clone the Workshop repository and run npm install (the tool needs @noble/hashes).

2. Write the bindings manifest {schema: "synthetic-d245bc86d584", sources: [{id, path (absolute), blake3}], quotes: [{id, source_id, text, byte_start, byte_end}]} from your sources and quotes: the BLAKE3 each source had when you quoted it and the UTF-8 byte range of each quote.

3. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:check-quotes-against-their-source-bytes"} and runs: node tools/pin-files-by-content/do-work/verify-source-spans.mjs --data bindings.json --out report.json. The report file must not exist yet; it is never replaced.

4. Read the line it prints ({status, sources, quotes, failures}); exit 0 is passed, 1 failed, 2 invalid or unreadable. The report lists each failure by kind and zero-based position, such as quote_literal_mismatch with literal_present_elsewhere.
5. A pass says only that the bytes match: it does not say who said it or what it means.

worked_examples.title: One quote matches its bytes and one does not
worked_examples.ask: Check the two quotes in bindings.json against menu.txt.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/pin-files-by-content/do-work/verify-source-spans.mjs and run on synthetic files: /work/menu.txt holds the 37 bytes "Fresh bread at seven. Closed Mondays." with BLAKE3 a86fa0567017461a7b411ef1be3202179c06d1a4b08b6146cca59eb2b8651741. bindings.json has one source (id menu) and two quotes on bytes 22 to 37: q1 with text "Closed Mondays." and q2 with text "Closed Sundays.". The AI runs: node tools/pin-files-by-content/do-work/verify-source-spans.mjs --data bindings.json --out report.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"status":"failed","sources":1,"quotes":2,"failures":1} with exit 1. report.json holds quotes[0].passed true and quotes[1].passed false, and failures [{"kind":"quote_literal_mismatch","quote_index":1,"literal_present_elsewhere":false}]; it names positions only, never paths, ids or text. The source row shows hash_matches true and bytes 37.
